sampling.sampling: Reservoir of up to 600 rows; first twelve byte-preview rows retained in discovery. Duplicate-content rows share one partition and are deduplicated.

inspection.grain: One row per party-activity record: a single party (party_activity.party_id, with party_activity.abn where supplied) in a single role (party_activity.party_role_category / party_activity.party_role) on a single IP right application (party_activity.ip_right_type + party_activity.application_number). The application-level columns (patent.application_number, patent.standard_complete, patent.status, patent.filing_date, patent.earliest_priority_date, patent.grant_date, patent.termination_date, patent.description) repeat for every party row on the same application, so a row is not one application and not one party; the same party can appear on many applications and the same application on many rows. The description table contributes at most one description per application, so it does not multiply rows.
identity_cautions: party_activity.abn is frequently blank (e.g. foreign organisations, individuals, agents); absence of an ABN must not be read as absence of a business or as a non-Australian entity.
party_activity.party_name is free text and lower-cased; the same organisation may appear under name variants, and a personal name must not be used to infer a company legal form or an ABN.

party_activity.party_id is the party key, but party_role_category/party_role distinguish applicant, patentee, agent, opponent etc.; the same party_id can hold different roles across rows, so party_id alone does not identify a unique business relationship.
party_activity.party_type (organisation/individual) is a party classification, not a company legal form or beneficial-ownership statement.
party_activity.state_code, post_code and country_code are party address attributes; post_code values are not uniformly formatted (e.g. 'gu14 0lx' vs '2106') and country_code is not always present.

patent.status, patent.filing_date, patent.earliest_priority_date, patent.grant_date, patent.termination_date and patent.description describe the application, not the party or the business; a grant date is not a business incorporation date and a status is not a business fact.
party_activity.effective_from_date / effective_to_date / is_current describe the party-role record's validity, not the application's or the business's lifecycle.
The cohort is a patent-prefix subset, not a population sample; no population-level accuracy or completeness claim can be made.
Model-proposed joins were checked on full right tables and missing/ambiguous matches are null, so blank application-level fields may reflect an unmatched join rather than a true absence of data.
inspection.rationale: The bytes are plain UTF-8 (BOM present, hence utf-8-sig) text with a consistent 29 commas per line across the sampled lines, so a comma-delimited reader with no skipped rows is the correct shared reader; the first line is the header. The header is a flat, prefixed set of column groups: party_activity.* (party identity, role, address, validity), patent.* (application identity, type, status, dates, description), and further prefixed groups visible in the truncated header. Sheet names are not applicable because this is a CSV, not a workbook, so no documentation sheet is involved. No nested singleton objects are present in this flat delimited file, so no bindings are proposed. Dates are ISO-8601 timestamps with a Z suffix and are contextual to the application or party-role record as noted; no percentage-encoded columns are visible in the sampled header or rows, so no percentage-storage note applies.

entity_types.name: party

entity_types.definition: An IP right application identified by ip_right_type plus application_number, carrying its own status, dates and description.

entity_types.name: party_activity

relationship_types.name: PARTY_ACTS_ON_APPLICATION

history.name: party_identity
history.purpose: Identity and classification of the party named on the record: party key, name, party type, and the ABN where supplied. Party type is a party classification, not a legal form.

findings: Held-out validation shows 110/110 records emitted for party_key, party_name and party_kind with 0 rejected values, and 47/110 for abn_supplied with 0 rejected values; the 63 blanks are deliberate abstention on a frequently-missing source attribute, not incorrect emissions.

Semantic separation is defensible: party_key is explicitly not an ABN/ACN or legal-entity assertion; party_name is explicitly not a registered legal or trading name; party_kind is explicitly a party classification with no legal-form, sole-trader or beneficial-ownership implication; abn_supplied is explicitly unvalidated and its absence is explicitly not evidence of no business or no Australian presence.

Owner separation is correct: all four concepts are owned by the party role, not by business, so entity.abn, entity.acn, entity.legal_name, entity.trading_name, entity.entity_type, ext.entity.legal_form and ext.entity.holder_kind are not reused where reuse would change meaning or owner.

Grain and identity cautions are consistent with the inspection: party_id alone does not identify a unique business relationship (roles vary across rows), and application-level status/dates/description are correctly excluded from this group's columns.
Enum mapping is bounded: only 'organisation' and 'individual' map, with unlisted values becoming missing rather than guessed; held-out examples confirm both values pass through unchanged.

Privacy handling is honest: party_name is marked personal_data=always and the mapping rationale states it is suppressed from profile views for the mixed person/organisation population, with the lost utility acknowledged rather than hidden.
No population-accuracy or completeness claim is made; the cohort is described as a patent-prefix subset and the quality gate note states it does not establish semantic truth or useful coverage.
No invented fallback dates or hypothetical guards are required; observed_at uses resource_last_modified fallback, which is observation-at-retrieval and is not described as a publisher-stated update.
semantic_risks: party_name values in held-out examples include digit strings (e.g. '2611463834', '9010020818') classified as individual parties; these are party labels as published, not names, and downstream consumers must not treat them as person names or as identifiers.
abn_supplied is stored as a string without checksum validation; a non-11-digit or malformed supplied value would pass through unchanged, so consumers must not treat it as a validated ABN.
party_kind is a party classification only; a value of 'organisation' must not be read as a company legal form, and 'individual' must not be read as sole-trader status.

party_key is a publisher party identifier; the same organisation may appear under multiple party_ids and the same party_id may hold different roles across rows, so it must not be used as a business entity key.
The 42.7% coverage on abn_supplied reflects source blanks, not a mapping defect; any downstream completeness metric must not interpret the blanks as absence of an Australian business.
checked_reuse: entity.abn — rejected: validated business-owned identifier; abn_supplied is unvalidated, often-missing party-record attribute whose absence is not evidence.
entity.acn — rejected: checksummed company registration with different owner and meaning than an IP-office party key.
entity.legal_name — rejected: asserts registered legal name; party_name is an unverified, lower-cased IP-office party label.
entity.trading_name — rejected: asserts trading status; party_name makes no such assertion.
entity.entity_type — rejected: asserts business legal structure; party_kind is a party-level organisation/individual flag with no legal-form implication.
ext.entity.legal_form — rejected: asserts business legal form; party_kind explicitly does not.
ext.entity.holder_kind — rejected: business-owned matching evidence about a licence/registration holder, a different meaning and owner than a party classification on an IP application record.
critic.rationale: The group's four concepts are semantically defensible, correctly owned by the party role, and explicitly bounded against legal-form, legal-identity, validation and population claims. Held-out validation shows full coverage with zero rejected values on the three fully-present fields and honest partial coverage (47/110) on the frequently-blank ABN field, with blanks treated as deliberate abstention rather than incorrect emissions. Reuse checks confirm that business-owned identifiers and legal-form concepts were not inappropriately reused. No blocking semantic, owner, unit, date, legal-claim or provenance defect was found in the emitted claims; the remaining risks are consumer-interpretation cautions, not mapping or ontology errors. This is an automated critique, not human approval.

history.name: party_role_on_application
history.purpose: The role the party holds on the application (applicant, patentee, agent, opponent, mortgagee etc.) and the validity window of that party-role record. These describe the party-role record, not the application or the business lifecycle.

findings: All six proposed concepts are owned by party_activity and their definitions consistently scope the values to the party-role record, explicitly excluding application status/dates and business lifecycle/incorporation.

Held-out validation shows 0.0 error rate of present values for all six fields; role_category, role, is_founding, is_current and effective_from_date each cover 110/110 records, and effective_to_date covers 24/110 present values (0.218) with blanks treated as missing rather than fabricated dates.

Enum mappings are closed (passthrough false, default null), so unlisted publisher categories/roles are withheld rather than coerced; observed values (applicant, applicant_agent, applicant, patentee, agent, true/false) all fall inside the declared value sets.
Date parsing accepts ISO-8601 Z timestamps and plain dates; effective_to_date applies null_if before parse_date so blank open-ended roles are abstentions, not dates.

Grain is correctly stated as one party-activity record (party in a role on an application), with application-level columns acknowledged as repeating; the party_activity key includes party_id, role_category, role, application_number and ip_right_type, which is consistent with the caution that party_id alone does not identify a unique relationship.
No legal-form, ABN, ownership, beneficial-interest or enforceability claims are emitted; is_founding is explicitly framed as a party-role flag, not an establishment date or incorporation evidence.
The cohort is described as a patent-prefix subset with no population accuracy claim, and the quality note correctly disclaims semantic truth.
semantic_risks: is_founding is a publisher flag whose exact semantics (founding of what, relative to which entity) are not documented in the supplied evidence; the definition is defensible as a party-role attribute but downstream consumers could still misread it as business establishment. The definition's explicit prohibition mitigates but does not eliminate this.

effective_from_date examples include 2026-04-16, a future-dated value relative to the 2026-11-23 retrieval; this is plausibly a publisher-recorded role start, but it should not be interpreted as an event that has occurred in the business's history.

party_role_category and party_role are near-duplicates; the finer role (patentee, opponent) is not always derivable from the category (applicant, opposition), so both are retained, but consumers may double-count roles if they treat them as independent facts.
effective_to_date coverage of 0.218 reflects genuine open-ended roles; absence of an end date must not be read as the role having ended or the business having ceased.
checked_reuse: ext.licence.category / ext.licence.status — rejected: owned by licence, describes an authorisation, not a party's role on an application.
ext.licence.start_date / ext.licence.end_date — rejected: owned by licence, not the validity window of a party-role association.
ext.entity.date_established — rejected: owned by business and a date, whereas is_founding is a boolean party-role flag; reuse would change owner, type and meaning.
critic.rationale: The group's six concepts are semantically defensible: each is owned by party_activity, scoped to the party-role record, and explicitly separated from application-level status/dates and from business establishment or legal form. Held-out validation shows zero error rate of present values across all six fields, with honest partial coverage on effective_to_date (0.218) reflecting genuinely blank open-ended roles rather than fabricated dates. Enum mappings are closed and withhold unlisted values, and date parsing handles the observed ISO-8601 Z format with blank-to-null handling. No legal-form, ABN, ownership or enforceability claims are made, and the cohort is correctly described as a non-population patent-prefix subset. Residual risks (undocumented is_founding semantics, future-dated effective_from_date, category/role near-duplication) are documented as semantic risks rather than blocking defects, since the definitions already bound their meaning. No blocking findings; repair_scope none.

fields.rationale: party_activity.party_role_category is the publisher's broad role category on the party-role record; maps to the party_activity-owned role_category concept. Unlisted categories are withheld rather than passed through.
party_activity.party_role is the specific role the party holds on the application; maps to the party_activity-owned role concept. Unlisted roles are withheld.
Boolean founding flag on the party-role record; kept as a party_activity attribute, not a business establishment date.
Boolean currency flag on the party-role record; describes the role association's validity, not the application or business lifecycle.
Publisher-stated start of the party-role validity window; an independently reported date owned by the party-activity record, not the application filing date or business establishment.
Publisher-stated end of the party-role validity window, frequently blank for open-ended roles; blank is treated as missing, not as a date.

history.name: party_address
history.purpose: Address attributes of the party as recorded on the record: country, state and post code. Post code formats are not uniform and country is not always present.

findings: All three proposed concepts (dyn.party.address_country, dyn.party.address_state, dyn.party.address_postcode) are owned by the party role, not the business subject, and their definitions explicitly disclaim incorporation, registered office, operating region and Australian-only scope.

findings: Application-level dates (application_date, earliest_filed_date, priority_date, registration_status_date, enforceable_status_date, deemed_retired_date) map cleanly to ip_application-owned concepts with 0.0 error rate on present values; meanings are correctly scoped to the application, not the party or business.

The status enum is the only failing field: 50 of 110 present values are rejected as INVALID_ENUM_VALUE_INVALID with examples 'unknown', 'withdrawn', 'expired'. The mapping uses map_enum with passthrough=true, but the concept declares a closed four-value enum (filed, accepted, granted, lapsed), so passthrough values outside the enum are rejected by the technical gate.

The concept definition itself acknowledges the value list is not the publisher's complete vocabulary, yet the enum is closed; this is an internal inconsistency between the declared enum and the passthrough mapping.

registration_status_date and enforceable_status_date are application milestones; they must not be read as business registration or current enforceability, which the definitions correctly exclude.

findings: Grain is correctly stated: one row per party-activity record, with application-level columns repeating across party rows; the group does not claim one row per application or per party.

Date parsing formats (%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ, %Y-%m-%d) match the observed ISO-8601 Z-suffixed raw values; held-out examples (e.g. 2001-07-06T00:00:00.000Z -> 2001-07-06) confirm correct date extraction.

application.enforceable_from_date is honestly unmapped with an explicit reason (column entirely empty, 0 nonempty of 381) rather than mapped to emit nothing or imply enforceability; the concept is retained for schema completeness only, which is a defensible abstention.

semantic_risks: The ip_application key is (application.application_number, application.ip_right_type); if the same application_number ever appears under two ip_right_type values, two distinct application entities would be created. No evidence of collision is shown, but the key is composite and should be treated as such.

Application-level columns repeat across party rows, so downstream aggregation must deduplicate by application key before counting applications; the group states this but the mapping does not enforce it.

Dates such as 2026-04-16 (registration/enforceable status) and 2025-11-13 (deemed retired) are later than the retrieved_at of 2026-11-23? No — they precede it, but future-dated milestones relative to typical publication should be sanity-checked against the snapshot; they are publisher-stated values and are emitted as such, not as business facts.

The record_id strategy is content_hash with empty source_paths and empty rationale; this is an experiment-level envelope choice, not a semantic claim, but it means record identity is not tied to the application key.

concepts.definition: Publisher's identifier for the party named on an IP right application record (party_activity.party_id). Identifies the party across applications and roles; it is not a business registration number, ABN or ACN, and does not by itself establish a legal entity.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an IP-office party key; entity.abn and entity.acn are checksummed business/company registrations with different owners and meaning, and entity.legal_name is a registered name, not an identifier.

concepts.definition: Party name as published on the IP right application record (party_activity.party_name), free text and lower-cased. It may be an organisation name variant or a personal name; it is not asserted to be a registered legal name or a trading name.
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.legal_name and entity.trading_name are owned by business and assert registered/trading status; this value is an unverified IP-office party label owned by the party role, so reuse would change meaning and owner.

concepts.definition: Publisher's classification of the party on the IP right application record as an organisation or an individual (party_activity.party_type). This is a party classification only; it does not state a company legal form, sole-trader status or beneficial ownership.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.holder_kind is owned by business and is matching evidence about a licence/registration holder; entity.entity_type and ext.entity.legal_form assert business legal structure. A party-level organisation/individual flag with no legal-form implication is a distinct meaning on a different owner.

concepts.definition: Australian Business Number as supplied on the IP right application party record (party_activity.abn), recorded as an 11-digit string. It is frequently blank, and a blank must not be read as absence of a business or of an Australian presence; it is not validated here and does not establish the party's legal identity.
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.abn is owned by business and is defined as a validated business identifier; this value is an unvalidated, often-missing party-record attribute whose absence is not evidence, so reuse would change meaning, owner and validation scope.

concepts.definition: Publisher's broad category of the role the party holds on the IP right application record (party_activity.party_role_category), e.g. applicant, applicant_agent, opposition, mortgagee. Describes the party-role record only; it does not imply ownership, beneficial interest or enforceability of the application.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an IP-office party-role category; ext.licence.category and ext.licence.status are owned by licence and describe an authorisation, not a party's role on an application, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher's specific role the party holds on the IP right application record (party_activity.party_role), e.g. applicant, patentee, agent, opponent. A finer-grained companion to the role category; it describes the party-role record, not the application or the business lifecycle.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept expresses a party's specific role on an IP application; ext.licence.category is a licence category owned by licence, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher's flag on the party-role record stating whether the party is recorded as founding (party_activity.is_founding, true/false). It is a party-role attribute and must not be read as a business establishment date or as evidence of incorporation.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.date_established is a business establishment date owned by business; a boolean founding flag on a party-role record has a different owner, type and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher's flag stating whether the party-role record is currently valid (party_activity.is_current, true/false). It describes the validity of the party-role association, not the application's status or the business's lifecycle.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.status is a licence status owned by licence; a boolean currency flag on a party-role record has a different owner, type and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated start of the validity window of the party-role record (party_activity.effective_from_date). It is the commencement of the party's role association on the application, not the application filing/priority date and not the business establishment date.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.start_date is owned by licence and ext.entity.date_established is owned by business; neither covers the validity start of a party-role association, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated end of the validity window of the party-role record (party_activity.effective_to_date), frequently blank when the role is open-ended. It is the end of the party's role association on the application, not the application termination date and not the end of the business.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.end_date is owned by licence and describes a licence's end; the end of a party-role association has a different owner and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Country component of the address recorded for the party on the IP right application record (party_activity.country_code), as published and lower-cased (e.g. 'au', 'us', 'cn'). It is frequently blank, and a blank must not be read as an Australian address or as absence of a country. It is a party-record address attribute, not a statement of the party's place of incorporation or of the business's registered office.
concepts.why_not_existing: address.country is owned by business and describes the business's own stated address; this value is an unverified, often-missing address attribute of an IP-office party record, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: State or province component of the address recorded for the party on the IP right application record (party_activity.state_code), as published and lower-cased (e.g. 'nsw', 'vic'). Values are not restricted to Australian states and are frequently blank; it is a party-record address attribute, not a business operating region or a statement of incorporation.
concepts.why_not_existing: address.state is owned by business, is an enum of Australian/NZ/OTHER codes and describes the business's own address; this raw, lower-cased, non-Australian-only party-record value has a different owner and scope, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Post code component of the address recorded for the party on the IP right application record (party_activity.post_code), kept as the raw published string because formats are not uniform (e.g. '2106' vs 'gu14 0lx'). It is a party-record address attribute and is not normalised to an Australian postcode.
concepts.why_not_existing: address.postcode is owned by business and describes the business's own address; this unnormalised, mixed-format party-record value has a different owner and no guaranteed Australian scope, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher's identifier for the IP right application (application.application_number, repeated as party_activity.application_number), as published. It identifies the application only in combination with the IP right type; it is not a business registration number, ABN or ACN, and does not identify the party or the business.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an IP-office application number; ext.licence.number and ext.licence.related_licence_number are owned by licence and identify authorisations, and ext.entity.prior_registration_number is a legacy business registration number, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher's classification of the kind of IP right the application seeks (application.ip_right_type, repeated as party_activity.ip_right_type), e.g. patent. It classifies the application, not the party or the business, and does not state that any right has been granted or is enforceable. The value list reflects the patent-prefix cohort in this snapshot and is not a general IP-right-type vocabulary.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept classifies an IP right application; ext.licence.category and ext.licence.authorisation are owned by licence and describe an authorisation held by a business, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher's sub-classification of the IP right application within its IP right type (application.ip_right_sub_type). For patents the observed vocabulary includes standard_complete, innovation, provisional and petty; the list is not asserted to be exhaustive of the publisher's vocabulary. It describes the application's own category and does not imply grant, enforceability or a business attribute.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept expresses an application sub-type; ext.licence.category is a licence category owned by licence, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated lifecycle status of the IP right application (application.status), e.g. filed, accepted, granted, lapsed, withdrawn, expired, ceased, unknown. It describes the application's own administrative state at the snapshot; it is not a business status, not evidence of grant or enforceability beyond the stated value, and not a statement about any party. 'ceased' is a publisher-stated application lifecycle state and must not be read as business cessation or as a party's status; 'unknown' is a legitimate publisher-stated state, not a parse failure.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.status is owned by licence and describes an authorisation held by a business; an IP-office application status has a different owner, subject and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date the IP right application was filed/lodged (application.application_date). It is the application's own filing date, not the party-role validity start, not the business establishment date and not a registration date.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.start_date is owned by licence and ext.entity.date_established is owned by business; neither covers the filing date of an IP right application, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated earliest filing date recorded for the IP right application (application.earliest_filed_date), which may precede the current application's own filing date where an earlier filing is carried forward. It is an application-level date, not the party-role validity start and not a business date.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an earliest-filing date of an IP application; ext.licence.start_date and ext.entity.date_established have different owners and meanings, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated priority date of the IP right application (application.priority_date), the date from which priority is claimed. It is an application-level legal date, not the filing date, not a grant date and not a business date.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept expresses a priority date; ext.licence.start_date and ext.entity.date_established are owned by licence and business respectively, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date on which the IP right application gained registered status (application.gained_registration_status_date). Frequently blank; a blank must not be read as 'never registered'. It is an application-level milestone, not a business incorporation or registration date.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.date_established and ext.entity.prior_registration_state concern business establishment/registration; a registration milestone of an IP application has a different owner and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date on which the IP right application gained enforceable status (application.gained_enforceable_status_date). Frequently blank; a blank must not be read as 'not enforceable'. It is an application-level milestone and does not assert that any right is in fact enforceable against any party.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an enforceability milestone of an IP application; ext.licence.start_date/end_date are licence validity dates with a different owner and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date from which the IP right application is enforceable (application.enforceable_from_date). The column is entirely empty in this snapshot, so the concept is defined for schema completeness only and no value is asserted; it is not the same as the date enforceable status was gained.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an enforceability start date of an IP application, and ext.licence.start_date is a licence validity start owned by licence, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date on which the IP right application is deemed retired (application.deemed_retired_date). Frequently blank; a blank must not be read as 'still active'. It is an application-level date, not the end of a party-role association and not the end of the business.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.end_date is owned by licence and dyn.party_activity.effective_to_date is owned by party_activity; a deemed-retirement date of an IP application has a different owner and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

available_concepts.definition: Australian Business Number. Has a checksum — validate it, do not just length-check.
As registered. Not the trading name.

mapping.record_grain: One row per party-activity record: a single party (party_activity.party_id, with party_activity.abn where supplied) in a single role (party_activity.party_role_category / party_activity.party_role) on a single IP right application (party_activity.ip_right_type + party_activity.application_number). Application-level columns repeat for every party row on the same application, so a row is neither one application nor one party.
mapping.grain_rationale: Model-authored grain and groups; executable envelope compiled deterministically.

fields.rationale: Publisher's party identifier on the party-activity record; identifies the party across applications and roles, not a business registration number.

Free-text, lower-cased party label as published. Not asserted to be a registered legal name or trading name; personal_data=always so it is suppressed from profile views for the mixed person/organisation population.
Publisher's organisation/individual party classification only; no legal-form, sole-trader or beneficial-ownership inference. Unlisted values become missing rather than guessed.

ABN as supplied on the party record, kept as a string without checksum validation because the concept is explicitly unvalidated; blanks are frequent and must not be read as absence of a business or Australian presence. Not mapped to entity.abn, which is a validated business-owned identifier.

party_activity.party_role_category is the publisher's broad role category on the party-role record; maps to the party_activity-owned role_category concept. Unlisted categories are withheld rather than passed through.
party_activity.party_role is the specific role the party holds on the application; maps to the party_activity-owned role concept. Unlisted roles are withheld.
Boolean founding flag on the party-role record; kept as a party_activity attribute, not a business establishment date.
Boolean currency flag on the party-role record; describes the role association's validity, not the application or business lifecycle.
Publisher-stated start of the party-role validity window; an independently reported date owned by the party-activity record, not the application filing date or business establishment.
Publisher-stated end of the party-role validity window, frequently blank for open-ended roles; blank is treated as missing, not as a date.

Country component of the party's recorded address on the IP right application record; owned by the party role, not the business's own address. Kept as published (lower-cased) with blanks treated as missing rather than as an Australian address.

State/province component of the party's recorded address. Not restricted to Australian states and frequently blank, so it is mapped to the party-owned raw state concept rather than the business-owned address.state enum; no state normalisation is applied to avoid asserting an Australian scope.

Post code component of the party's recorded address, kept as the raw published string because formats are not uniform ('2106' vs 'gu14 0lx'). The postcode transform is deliberately not applied since it would force a 4-digit Australian assumption the source does not support.

The publisher's application number for the application. party_activity.application_number is the same value repeated on every party row of the same application, so it is not joined (joining produced duplicated identifiers); it is declined as a redundant repetition of this column. The number identifies the application only together with the IP right type.

Classifies the kind of IP right applied for; the observed value is 'patent'. party_activity.ip_right_type repeats the same application-level value and is declined as redundant (joining it produced 'patent patent', which failed the enum map). This classifies the application, not the party or the business, and does not assert grant or enforceability.

The sub-type column classifies the application within its IP right type. The observed vocabulary includes 'petty' in addition to standard_complete, innovation and provisional, so it is mapped explicitly rather than silently dropped; any other unlisted value yields no claim. It is an application attribute, not a business attribute.

application.status is the publisher's lifecycle status of the IP right application; dyn.ip_application.status is owned by ip_application and enumerates the observed publisher vocabulary including 'ceased', which is a publisher-stated application lifecycle state and must not be read as business cessation or as a party's status. passthrough is disabled so any unlisted value is withheld rather than emitted against an incomplete enum. It is not a business status, so it is attached to the ip_application role, not the subject.

application.application_date is the application's own filing/lodging date, matching dyn.ip_application.application_date (owner ip_application). It is not a business establishment date or a party-role validity start.

application.earliest_filed_date is the earliest filing date recorded for the application, matching dyn.ip_application.earliest_filed_date. It is an application-level date, distinct from the current filing date and from any business date.
application.priority_date is the priority date claimed for the application, matching dyn.ip_application.priority_date. It is a legal date of the application, not a grant or business date.

application.gained_registration_status_date is the date the application gained registered status, matching dyn.ip_application.registration_status_date. Blank values are left missing and must not be read as 'never registered'; it is not a business registration date.

application.gained_enforceable_status_date is the date the application gained enforceable status, matching dyn.ip_application.enforceable_status_date. It is an application milestone and does not assert actual enforceability; blanks stay missing.

application.deemed_retired_date is the date the application is deemed retired, matching dyn.ip_application.deemed_retired_date. It is an application-level date, not the end of a party-role association or of the business; blanks stay missing.

application_description.application_number and application_description.ip_right_type link the description to the application; the description table contributes at most one description per application.

step.meaning: Each reported party role row on a right is matched to the single application record for the same right type and application number, so analysts can attach source-stated status and dates to each party role.
cautions: Composite key required because application numbers are scoped by ip_right_type; joining on application_number alone could match a different right type.
Assumes application is unique per (ip_right_type, application_number); duplicates in the full right table will cause the join to be refused rather than silently deduplicated.
Party role presence does not imply ownership, entitlement, or current enforceability of the right.
Status and dates are source-stated values, not derived legal conclusions.

measurement.scope: Key/cardinality checks cover the supplied anchor cohort, not all business identities.

step.meaning: Each party role row is matched to the description record for the same right type and application number, giving a human-readable description of the right alongside the party role.
cautions: Only valid as many_to_one if application_description holds at most one row per (ip_right_type, application_number); the schema includes description_type, so multiple description types per application would break this and the join must be refused.
If multiple description types exist, a description_type filter (e.g. 'description') would be needed, which is a selection not a star join.
Description text is source-stated and may be truncated or absent; it is not a legal scope of the right.

source.title: ACNC 2024 Annual Information Statement (AIS) Data
source.notes:
This dataset is updated weekly. Please ensure that you use the most up-to-date version.

###Background###
The Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) is Australia’s national regulator of charities. Since 3 December 2012, charities wanting to access Commonwealth charity tax concessions (and other benefits) need to register with the ACNC. Although many charities choose to register, registration with the ACNC is voluntary.

Each year, registered charities are required to lodge an Annual Information Statement (AIS) with the ACNC. Charities are required to submit their AIS within six months of the end of their reporting period.

The AIS collects information about a charity’s programs, HR and financial information.

###AIS data###
This dataset can be used to find 2024 AIS information lodged by multiple charities.

It can also be used to filter and sort by different variables across all AIS information. AIS Information for individual charities can be viewed via the ACNC Charity Register.

Our explanatory notes (see below) detail the information collected in the AIS and the data outputs you can expect.

The ACNC has also published a report analysing 2024 AIS data. This report - the 12th edition of the Charities Report - can be found on our website.

###Interpreting AIS data###
When comparing charities’ financial information it is important to consider each charity's unique situation. This is particularly true for small charities, which are not compelled to provide financial reports – reports that often contain more details about their financial position and activities – as part of their AIS. For more information on interpreting financial information, please refer to the ACNC website.

###Withheld information###
Registered charities can apply to the ACNC to have some or all of the information they provide withheld from the ACNC Register. However, there are only limited circumstances when the ACNC can agree to withhold information. If a charity has applied to have their data withheld, the AIS data relating to that charity has been excluded from this dataset.

NOTE: It is possible that some information in this dataset might be subject to a future request from a charity to have their information withheld. If this occurs, this information will still appear in the dataset until the next update. Please consider this risk when using this dataset.

###More ACNC data###
The ACNC also publishes other datasets on data.gov.au as part of our commitment to open data and transparent regulation.

sampling.sampling: Reservoir of up to 600 rows; first twelve byte-preview rows retained in discovery. Duplicate-content rows share one partition and are deduplicated.

inspection.grain: One row per charity (identified by ABN) for the 2024 Annual Information Statement reporting year, carrying that charity's registration details, AIS lodgement dates, activity descriptions, staffing/volunteer counts, financial-report classification and reported financial figures for its own reporting period (period start/end dates appear as separate columns, so the financial figures are period-specific rather than calendar-2024).
identity_cautions: ABN is the only stable identifier; charity name is free text and may vary in case, punctuation and legal suffix, so names must not be used as a join key.
ABN is stored as a bare digit string with no separators and may lose leading structure if coerced to a number; keep it as text.

The file is a single flat CSV with no header groups or multi-row headers; the header row is row 1 and every subsequent row is a data record. Quoted fields contain commas and semicolons, so a naive split on commas will misalign columns.
Financial figures relate to each charity's own reporting period (start/end date columns), not a common 1 July–30 June year; comparing amounts across rows without checking those dates is unsafe.

Charity size (Small/Medium/Large) is a reporting classification, not a measure of company scale or legal form, and small charities are not required to supply detailed financials, so blanks and zeros are not evidence of nil activity.
Registration status and AIS due/received dates describe regulatory lodgement, not business incorporation or a licence date.

Percentage-like and count-like columns (e.g. staffing/volunteer counts, financial breakdowns) are stored as plain numbers without units or percent signs; storage as a fraction versus a whole-number percentage cannot be confirmed from the visible bytes and must be checked per column before use.
Some charities have withheld information and are excluded from the dataset, so absence of a row is not evidence a charity does not exist.
The dataset is refreshed weekly; the local snapshot is a point-in-time copy and later versions may differ.
inspection.rationale: The bytes are plain UTF-8 text (BOM present, hence utf-8-sig) with a comma delimiter: the first line is a single header row of ~90+ comma-separated field names beginning 'abn,charity name,registration status,...', and data lines show the same comma count with quoted fields containing embedded commas. There is no ZIP container, no workbook and no documentation sheet, so a delimited reader with skip_rows 0 and comma delimiter is the correct shared reader; no sheet name needs preserving and no nested objects exist to bind. Header groups are absent (flat single header), and the identifier caution is that ABN, not the free-text charity name, is the row key. Contextual years appear as AIS due/received dates and per-charity reporting period start/end dates rather than a single dataset year column, and percentage storage is not visibly marked, so both are flagged as cautions rather than assumed.

entity_types.name: charity
entity_types.definition: A registered charity lodging an Annual Information Statement with the ACNC, identified by its ABN; its legal form is not inferred from its name.

entity_types.name: fundraising_authorisation
entity_types.definition: A state or territory fundraising registration/licence number held by a charity, evidenced by a fundraising number column for that jurisdiction.

charity.rationale: ABN is the only stable identifier for the row subject; charity name is free text and must not be used as a key.

fundraising_authorisation.rationale: Each populated fundraising number column evidences a jurisdiction-specific fundraising registration held by the charity; the number is the only identifier present.

relationship_types.name: HOLDS_FUNDRAISING_AUTHORISATION
relationship_types.definition: Charity holds a state or territory fundraising registration evidenced by a fundraising number column for that jurisdiction.

relationships.rationale: Fundraising number columns (act, nsw, qld, sa, tas, vic, wa) are populated only for charities holding that jurisdiction's fundraising registration; the corresponding fundraising flag columns indicate activity, not the authorisation itself.

cautions: ABN is the only stable identifier; charity name is free text and must not be used as a join key or to infer legal form.
Financial figures relate to each charity's own reporting period (fin report from/to), not a common financial year; cross-row comparison without checking those dates is unsafe.
Charity size (Small/Medium/Large) is a reporting classification, not company scale or legal form; blanks and zeros for small charities are not evidence of nil activity.
Registration status and AIS due/received dates describe regulatory lodgement, not business incorporation or a licence date.
Association numbers and fundraising numbers are state-specific registrations; their presence does not establish company legal form or a single national licence.
Numeric columns are stored without units or percent signs; fraction-versus-percentage storage cannot be confirmed from the visible bytes.
Some charities have withheld information and are excluded, so absence of a row is not evidence a charity does not exist.
The dataset is refreshed weekly; the local snapshot is a point-in-time copy.

findings: Held-out validation shows 0.0 error rate of present values for every emitted field across 140 validation records; no malformed values and no record errors.
entity.abn: 140/140 present, 140 emitted, checksum transform applied; ABN kept as text with pattern ^\d{11}$ — consistent with the identity caution that ABN must not be coerced to a number.

entity.legal_name: 140/140 emitted with claim_scope current_legal_name; examples (e.g. 'Chapter Seven Limited', 'PBCC Properties Katoomba LT 1 Trust') are registered charity names, not trading names, so the 'as registered' definition is defensible.

entity.website and ext.contact.website_domain: 93/140 present, 93 emitted (0.664 coverage). The 47 absent values are genuinely blank in source, so this is honest partial coverage, not a mapping defect. Domain derivation (www.chapterseven.au -> chapterseven.au) is correct.

dyn.charity.registration_status: 140/140 emitted; enum values match the four observed source strings exactly (Registered, Voluntarily Revoked No Longer Operating, etc.). Owner is charity, not business — correct separation from entity.status.

dyn.charity.basic_religious_charity and dyn.charity.incorporated_association: 140/140 emitted, y/n normalised via upper+map_enum; examples confirm 'n'/'y' round-trip. No legal-form inference from names is made.

dyn.charity.state_association_number: per-jurisdiction coverage (ACT 4, NSW 11, QLD 3, SA 6, VIC 18, WA 11, NT 0, TAS 0) matches source presence exactly; jurisdiction qualifier is set per column (e.g. A0710094Z -> WA, INC9875918 -> NSW). Zero-coverage jurisdictions (NT, TAS) are simply absent in the sample, not a mapping error.

Unmapped list correctly attributes all out-of-group columns (fundraising numbers, financials, staffing, AIS dates) to 'Outside this group; reconciled in the final source mapping' — no invented fallback values.
No population accuracy claim is made; quality note explicitly states the gate does not establish semantic truth or useful coverage.
semantic_risks: entity.legal_name claim_scope 'current_legal_name' is asserted for revoked charities (e.g. ordinal 561, 'Voluntarily Revoked No Longer Operating'). The name is the last registered name, which is defensible, but downstream consumers should not treat it as an active legal name without checking registration_status.

dyn.charity.state_association_number is multi-valued with a jurisdiction qualifier; the execution contract states arrays must be singletons, so each row emits at most one value per jurisdiction column. This is correct here but means a charity with multiple numbers in the same jurisdiction would be silently limited to one column value — acceptable given the source shape (one column per jurisdiction).
ext.contact.website_domain is owned by 'any' and multi=true; one value per row is emitted, which is consistent with the source but should not be read as exhaustive domain coverage for the charity.

Registration status enum is closed to four values; if the publisher introduces a new status string, map_enum passthrough=true would emit an out-of-enum value. This is a forward-compatibility risk, not a current defect.

ABN checksum transform is applied but the validation report does not show rejected ABNs; if any source ABNs fail checksum they would be dropped silently. No evidence of this in the 140 validation records (0 errors), but the behaviour is not observable from the report.
checked_reuse: entity.abn reused for 'abn' — same meaning (Australian Business Number) and same owner (business). Correct.
entity.legal_name reused for 'charity name' — registered name of the subject; owner business is the row subject, and the charity role is a facet of that subject. Defensible.
entity.website reused for 'charity website' — published website of the subject. Correct.
ext.contact.website_domain reused for derived domain — registrable host, owner 'any', multi=true. Correct.

history.name: fundraising_registrations
history.purpose: State-by-state and online fundraising activity flags together with the corresponding fundraising licence/registration numbers held by the charity.

findings: All 16 declared source columns in the group are mapped: 9 activity flags and 7 jurisdiction fundraising numbers; no group column is left unmapped.

Validation evidence shows 0.0 error rate of present values for every field, with full coverage (140/140) on all nine activity-flag columns and exact coverage of present values on all seven number columns (2, 12, 5, 4, 1, 5, 4).
Low coverage on number columns (e.g. TAS 1/140, ACT 2/140) reflects genuine sparsity of published fundraising numbers, not mapping loss; emitted counts equal source-present counts in every case.
Held-out examples confirm verbatim retention of jurisdiction-specific formats (FR0014958 for VIC, CFN/25582 and 13540 for NSW) with the correct jurisdiction qualifier attached.

Activity flags are correctly separated from numbers: ordinal 561 shows all 'n' flags with empty numbers, and ordinal 733 shows VIC 'y' with a VIC number, consistent with the stated relationship that flags indicate activity, not the authorisation itself.

The concept definition explicitly warns that a 'y' flag does not prove a registration number exists and that placeholder values like 00000 are not evidence of valid registration; this is an honest semantic bound rather than an overclaim.

Owner assignment to fundraising_authorisation (not charity or licence) is defensible: the number is jurisdiction-qualified and the flag is a per-jurisdiction activity indicator, neither of which is a charity attribute or a business licence.

Reuse rejections are correctly reasoned: state_association_number is a different regime (incorporated associations) and charity-owned; ext.licence.number is licence-owned; ext.licence.authorisation is text not a y/n flag; address.state is an address, not an activity indicator.
The 'online' literal used as the jurisdiction qualifier for the online column is explicitly documented in the concept definition, so it is a stated convention rather than an unmarked inference.
No legal-form, incorporation-date or licence-date claims are made from these columns; the group does not infer company legal form from names or ABNs.
The grain and identity cautions correctly note ABN as the only stable key and that absence of a row is not evidence a charity does not exist (withheld information).
semantic_risks: The 'online' value in the jurisdiction qualifier is a non-geographic literal mixed into a jurisdiction-qualified concept; consumers filtering by jurisdiction must know to treat 'online' specially, and a future concept split (e.g. a separate online-fundraising flag) may be cleaner.

The number concept is single-valued per jurisdiction, but the source has one column per jurisdiction, so a charity with multiple registrations in one jurisdiction could not be represented; the data does not appear to exhibit this, but the cardinality assumption is not evidenced.

Placeholder values such as 00000 are retained as published; downstream consumers may mistake them for valid registrations unless they read the concept definition, so the caveat lives only in documentation, not in the value.
Activity flags are self-reported AIS answers, not regulator-verified registrations; the concept definition says so, but any downstream use as proof of authorisation would be a semantic error.

The relationship HOLDS_FUNDRAISING_AUTHORISATION is declared but the execution contract emits edges only when both roles have claims; for charities with flags but no numbers, no authorisation edge will exist, which is correct but should not be read as 'no authorisation'.

The number columns are sparse (TAS 1/140), so any aggregate 'number of jurisdictions registered' derived from this group will undercount relative to flags; this is a coverage property, not a mapping error.

ext.licence.authorisation: correctly not reused — licence authorisation text, not a y/n activity flag.

history.name: workforce_and_volunteers
history.purpose: Staffing and volunteer headcounts reported by the charity, including full-time, part-time, casual and volunteer counts and total full-time-equivalent staff.

findings: All five workforce columns are present in every validation record (140/140) and 114/140 emit; the 26 non-emits per column are QUALIFIER_MISSING_PERIOD abstentions where 'fin report from' is blank, which is honest abstention rather than an incorrect value.
No malformed values: parse_integer/parse_decimal succeeded on all emitted values, including fractional FTE (0.3, 1.5) and published zeros (0 staff, 0 FTE).

Semantic split is defensible: paid staff headcount by employment_category, volunteers as a separate unpaid count, and FTE as a decimal workload-equivalent are three distinct meanings with distinct units; folding them would change meaning.
Owner is consistently 'charity' and the row subject is the charity keyed on ABN, matching the source grain of one row per charity.

The period qualifier is sourced from the charity's own 'fin report from' date, correctly reflecting period-specific rather than calendar-2024 figures; held-out rows show 01/01/2024 and 01/07/2023 periods, confirming the qualifier is not a fixed year.

The mapping's 'unmapped' list and the fundraising_authorisation entity/relationship are outside this group's five columns and are reconciled elsewhere; they do not affect the workforce claims under review.
semantic_risks: The 'period' qualifier carries only the period start date ('fin report from'), not the end date; a consumer could read it as a point-in-time observation rather than the start of a reporting window. This is a labelling risk, not a wrong value, since valid_from/valid_to are also bound.

Zeros are retained as published; for small charities not required to report detailed financials, a 0 headcount/FTE is a reported value and must not be read as evidence of no activity — the concept definitions state this, but downstream consumers must honour it.
Volunteer counts and staff headcounts are self-reported AIS figures with no independent verification; they are not audited headcounts.

dyn.charity.staff_headcount vs dyn.charity.full_time_equivalent_staff — kept separate: integer headcount of people vs decimal FTE workload-equivalent; merging would change units.
critic.rationale: The group's five workforce claims are semantically sound: correct owner (charity), correct units (people for headcounts, decimal FTE for the equivalent measure), period taken from each charity's own reporting period, and honest abstention (26/140 per column) where the period start is missing rather than invented. No malformed values and no incorrect emitted values are evidenced. The only issue warranting revision is a labelling/scope clarity point on the 'period' qualifier (start-only), which is a mapping/ontology clarification rather than a wrong value; coverage is honestly bounded and acceptable. No blocking findings are raised, so the verdict is revise for the qualifier-scope clarification rather than accept outright.

history.name: income_and_revenue
history.purpose: Reported income and revenue lines for the charity's own reporting period: total gross income, total revenue and its components (government, goods and services, investments, donations and bequests, other revenue, other income) plus other comprehensive income.

findings: All ten income/revenue concepts are charity-owned, period-qualified, AUD-qualified and correctly distinguished from business-owned ext.financial.total_income; the reuse refusal is defensible on owner and scope grounds.

The period qualifier is bound to 'fin report from' only, so the emitted period is a start date, not a period. Held-out row 561 shows fin report from 01/01/2024 and fin report to 16/08/2024, yet the emitted qualifier reads period=01/01/2024; row 733 reads period=01/07/2023 for a 01/07/2023-30/06/2024 period. The concept definitions promise 'its own financial reporting period', which the emitted qualifier does not carry.

The 26 withheld values per field (260 total, QUALIFIER_MISSING_PERIOD) are honest abstentions where the period start is absent; that is acceptable coverage, not an incorrect emission, and no fallback date should be invented.

Semantic separation of the ten lines is sound: total revenue vs total gross income (other income), other revenue vs other income, other comprehensive income vs total comprehensive income, and inbound donations/bequests vs outbound grants and donations made are all kept distinct.
Sign handling is correct: row 1018 other income -440 and row 733 net surplus -952 are retained by parse_decimal, consistent with the total comprehensive income definition allowing negatives.

The mapping's record_id uses content_hash with empty source_paths and empty rationale; the execution contract states a content hash is used regardless, so this is not a blocking defect, but the empty rationale is uninformative.

The mapping declares a fundraising_authorisation entity and HOLDS_FUNDRAISING_AUTHORISATION edge, but this group's proposal contains no fundraising concepts and no fields target that role; the edge can never emit from this group's claims. This is out of scope for the income group and should not be presented as part of its output.

The observed_at fallback is resource_last_modified, which the contract maps to retrieved_at when modification metadata is absent; this is observation-at-retrieval and must not be described as a publisher-stated update date.

No company legal form, incorporation date or licence date is inferred from ABN, name or registration status; the identity cautions correctly treat registration status and AIS dates as regulatory lodgement, not incorporation.
The 'charity size' classification is not used as a scale or legal-form claim, consistent with the identity cautions.
semantic_risks: Period qualifier carrying only the start date risks cross-row comparison of amounts from different-length reporting periods (e.g. a 7.5-month period vs a 12-month period) as if comparable.
Zero values in small-charity rows (e.g. row 561 all revenue components zero except donations) are reported figures, not evidence of nil activity; consumers must not read them as inactivity.
Withheld charities are excluded from the dataset, so absence of a row is not evidence a charity does not exist; coverage figures must not be read as population completeness.
The dataset is refreshed weekly; the local snapshot is point-in-time and later versions may differ.
checked_reuse: ext.financial.total_income: correctly not reused — business owner and aggregate scope differ from charity-role AIS lines.
ext.financial.taxable_income: correctly not reused — tax concept, not gross income.
dyn.charity.other_revenue vs dyn.charity.other_income: kept as separate concepts matching separate AIS columns; reuse would conflate meaning.
dyn.charity.other_comprehensive_income vs dyn.charity.total_comprehensive_income: kept separate; correct.
dyn.charity.donations_and_bequests_revenue vs outbound 'grants and donations made' columns: direction kept distinct; correct.
critic.rationale: The ten concepts are semantically defensible: charity-owned, AUD, period-specific, with revenue, other income and comprehensive income correctly separated and business-owned total income correctly refused. The blocking defect is that the required 'period' qualifier is bound only to 'fin report from', so emitted periods are start dates rather than reporting periods, contradicting the concepts' own definitions and the grain statement. The 26-per-field abstentions are honest missing-context abstentions, not incorrect values, and should be preserved. The fundraising entity/edge is out of scope for this group and should be removed from this group's mapping rather than repaired here. Repair is confined to mapping bindings; no ontology change is needed.

blocking_findings.field: dyn.charity.total_gross_income (and all nine sibling income concepts) qualifiers.period
blocking_findings.actual: period qualifier bound to source_path 'fin report from' only, emitting a start date such as period=01/01/2024 (row 561) and period=01/07/2023 (row 733)

The mapping's qualifiers.period declares source_path 'fin report from' with value null for every field.
blocking_findings.correction: In the mapping, change each field's qualifiers.period to bind both 'fin report from' and 'fin report to' (e.g. a period interval qualifier with start and end source paths, or two qualifier keys period_start/period_end), keeping the existing %d/%m/%Y validity_date_formats; retain QUALIFIER_MISSING_PERIOD abstention when either date is absent rather than inventing a fallback.

findings: Semantic meanings of the ten income/revenue concepts are defensible: each maps 1:1 to a distinct AIS column, owner is the charity role, and the definitions correctly separate revenue from other income and from other comprehensive income.
Reuse decision is sound: ext.financial.total_income is business-owned and does not distinguish revenue from other income, so declining reuse is correct rather than a coverage failure.

Coverage is honestly bounded: 114/140 validation rows emitted per field, with 26 abstentions per field all attributed to QUALIFIER_MISSING_PERIOD; no malformed values and no record errors. This is deliberate abstention, not an incorrect emitted value.

The period qualifier is populated from 'fin report from' only, so the emitted period is a start date, not a period. The concept requires a 'period' qualifier and the grain explicitly states figures are period-specific (start/end). A start date alone does not identify the reporting period and is semantically weaker than the declared qualifier.

The mapping declares valid_from_path and valid_to_path from 'fin report from'/'fin report to' with %d/%m/%Y, but the qualifier block only carries 'period' sourced from 'fin report from'. The end date is not represented in any qualifier, so the emitted claim cannot be reconstructed to a bounded period.

Held-out row 561 shows 'fin report from' 01/01/2024 and 'fin report to' 16/08/2024 — a non-standard, sub-annual period. Emitting only the start date would make this indistinguishable from a full calendar-year charity, which is a real semantic risk given the grain caution about non-common reporting years.

The 'period' qualifier value is null in the mapping while examples show a date string; the qualifier is populated at runtime from source_path, which is acceptable, but the concept's required_qualifiers list 'period' without specifying that it must be a bounded interval. This is a definitional gap, not a runtime error.
No legal-form, incorporation, licence or grant-amount claims are made; the concepts correctly avoid inferring company legal form from ABN or name. No population accuracy claim is made.

The fundraising_authorisation entity and HOLDS_FUNDRAISING_AUTHORISATION edge are outside this group's income scope and are not exercised by any income field; they are not a blocking issue for this group but should be reviewed by the owning group.
record_id uses content_hash with empty source_paths and empty rationale; this is an envelope concern, not a semantic income claim, and does not block this group.

observed_at uses fallback resource_last_modified; the execution contract says fallback uses retrieved_at if source modification metadata is absent. This is an envelope-level inconsistency, not a blocking semantic finding for income fields.
semantic_risks: Emitting only the reporting-period start date as the 'period' qualifier conflates a point date with a period; a consumer comparing amounts across charities could treat a 7.5-month period (row 561) as equivalent to a 12-month period.

The 'period' qualifier is required by the concept but its definition does not state it must be a closed interval (start and end); this invites future mappings to emit a single date and still pass the qualifier check.

Zero values are emitted as reported (e.g. revenue_from_government=0, other_income=0). The concept definitions correctly warn that zero is not evidence of nil activity, but downstream consumers may still misread zeros for small charities not required to report detailed financials.

total_comprehensive_income may be negative and parse_decimal retains signs; the definition notes this, but no example in the held-out set shows a negative total_comprehensive_income, so sign handling is asserted rather than demonstrated.

The 'period' qualifier source is 'fin report from' while valid_from/valid_to are declared separately; if the runtime only populates the qualifier from the start date, the end date is lost from the emitted claim even though the mapping declares it.
checked_reuse: ext.financial.total_income — correctly not reused: business owner, aggregate that does not separate revenue from other income, and no charity reporting period.
ext.financial.taxable_income — correctly not reused: tax concept, not gross income.
dyn.charity.other_revenue vs dyn.charity.other_income — correctly kept distinct: separate AIS columns ('all other revenue' vs 'other income').
dyn.charity.other_income vs dyn.charity.other_comprehensive_income — correctly kept distinct: different AIS lines and different accounting meaning.
dyn.charity.total_gross_income vs dyn.charity.total_revenue — correctly kept distinct: gross income includes other income, revenue does not.
dyn.charity.donations_and_bequests_revenue vs outbound 'grants and donations made' — correctly separated by direction; no reuse of an outflow concept for an inflow.
critic.rationale: The group's ten income/revenue concepts are semantically well-differentiated, correctly owned by the charity role, and correctly decline reuse of business-owned ext.financial.total_income. Coverage is honestly bounded (114/140 per field, 26 abstentions per field all QUALIFIER_MISSING_PERIOD) and no malformed values or record errors are reported, so the abstentions are deliberate and not incorrect emissions. The blocking issue is the period qualifier: the concept requires a 'period' qualifier, the grain states figures are period-specific with separate start/end columns, and held-out row 561 shows a non-standard 01/01/2024–16/08/2024 period. The mapping populates 'period' only from 'fin report from' (a start date) while declaring valid_from/valid_to separately, so the emitted claim does not carry a bounded period and a sub-annual period is indistinguishable from a full year. This is a mapping/ontology definitional gap that must be corrected before acceptance; the repair is to make 'period' a closed interval sourced from both 'fin report from' and 'fin report to' (or to add an explicit period_end qualifier) and to state in the concept definition that period is a bounded interval. Envelope-level issues (content_hash record_id with empty rationale, observed_at fallback naming) are noted but not blocking for this group's semantic claims. No human approval is implied by this critique.

blocking_findings.field: dyn.charity.total_gross_income (and all nine sibling income fields) — qualifiers.period
blocking_findings.actual: period qualifier sourced only from 'fin report from' (a start date), with valid_to_path 'fin report to' declared but not represented in any qualifier; concept required_qualifiers lists 'period' without defining it as a bounded interval.
blocking_findings.expected: period qualifier is a closed interval carrying both 'fin report from' and 'fin report to' (or an explicit period_end qualifier), and the concept definition states period is a bounded reporting interval, so a sub-annual period such as 01/01/2024–16/08/2024 is distinguishable from a full year.
blocking_findings.evidence: Held-out row 561 has 'fin report from' 01/01/2024 and 'fin report to' 16/08/2024 (a ~7.5-month period) while the emitted example shows qualifiers.period='01/01/2024' only; row 733 shows 01/07/2023–30/06/2024. The grain explicitly states figures are period-specific with separate start/end columns, and the concept requires a 'period' qualifier.
blocking_findings.correction: In the mapping, change the period qualifier to source both 'fin report from' and 'fin report to' (e.g. period_start from 'fin report from' and period_end from 'fin report to', or a single period interval value built from both), and in the ontology update dyn.charity.* income concept definitions to state that 'period' is a bounded reporting interval (start and end) rather than a single date. Re-run validation to confirm the 26 QUALIFIER_MISSING_PERIOD abstentions are re-evaluated against the bounded-interval requirement.
