concepts.definition: The ACNC registration status of the charity as published in the Annual Information Statement, including revocation reasons such as voluntary revocation or double defaulter. This is a charity-regulator status, not a company legal status or a licence status.
values: Voluntarily Revoked Not Entitled To Be A Charity
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.status is a coarse company-lifecycle enum (active/deregistered/in_liquidation/suspended/unknown) owned by business; ACNC charity registration states carry regulator-specific revocation reasons and belong to the charity role, so reuse would change meaning and owner. ext.licence.status is a licence status, not charity registration.

concepts.definition: Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity is a basic religious charity for the reporting year, recorded as y/n in the source.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers ACNC basic religious charity classification; ext.entity.tax_concession covers PBI/HPC/DGR concessions, a different regulatory attribute.

concepts.definition: Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity is an incorporated association, recorded as y/n. This is a self-reported association attribute, not an inference of legal form from the charity name.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept records incorporated-association status; entity legal form is not otherwise modelled and must not be inferred from names.

concepts.definition: State or territory incorporated-association registration number held by the charity, qualified by the jurisdiction whose association-number column supplied it. Values are publisher-formatted strings (e.g. INC9886754, A0005374L) and are not normalised across states.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.prior_registration_number is a single legacy state registration number with no jurisdiction qualifier and no multi-value scope; the ACNC file holds up to eight jurisdiction-specific association numbers per charity, so reuse would lose the jurisdiction and multiplicity. ext.entity.prior_registration_state is a state name, not a number.

concepts.definition: The type of modification the auditor or reviewer applied to the charity's financial report, as published by the ACNC (e.g. qualified/qualification, disclaimed/disclaimer, adverse). Only meaningful where the report modification flag is y; unlisted source labels are withheld rather than guessed.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept captures audit/review modification types; dyn.charity.report_modification_flag only records presence, not the modification kind. Enum extended to include the observed 'Adverse' label so genuine modification kinds are not withheld.

concepts.definition: Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity submitted its financial report to a cooperative or other regulator rather than to the ACNC (y/n), as recorded in the 'coop financial report submitted to regulator' column. A lodgement-channel indicator, not a registration status; the exact regulator and whether it replaces ACNC lodgement are not asserted.
source_paths: coop financial report submitted to regulator
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers alternative financial-report lodgement channels; dyn.charity.registration_status is a registration state, not a lodgement route. Definition narrowed to avoid over-specifying the regulator semantics.

concepts.definition: The date by which the charity's Annual Information Statement for the reporting year is due to be lodged with the ACNC, as published in the AIS dataset. This is a regulatory lodgement deadline, not a licence or registration date.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers ACNC AIS lodgement deadlines; ext.licence.start_date/end_date are licence validity dates owned by the licence role, and entity.date_registered is a business registration date, so reuse would change meaning and owner.

concepts.definition: The date on which the ACNC received the charity's Annual Information Statement for the reporting year, as published in the AIS dataset. This is a lodgement receipt date, not the charity's establishment or registration date.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept records AIS lodgement receipt; entity.date_registered and ext.entity.date_established are business dates with different meaning, and ext.licence dates belong to the licence role.

concepts.definition: The ACNC charity size classification (Small, Medium or Large) reported for the charity in its Annual Information Statement. This is a regulator reporting classification, not a measure of company scale, revenue band or legal form.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.financial.revenue_band is a revenue/turnover band from a named scheme owned by business; the ACNC size classification is a charity-role reporting category with its own thresholds and labels, so reuse would change meaning and owner.

concepts.definition: The start date of the reporting period covered by the charity's financial report as lodged with the ACNC. Defines the period scope for the charity's financial figures; it is not a registration or licence start date.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept captures a charity financial-reporting period boundary; ext.licence.start_date is a licence commencement owned by the licence role and entity.date_registered is a business registration date.

concepts.definition: The end date of the reporting period covered by the charity's financial report as lodged with the ACNC. Defines the period scope for the charity's financial figures; it is not a financial year-end attribute or a licence end date.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.financial_year_end is a recurring dd-Mon reporting-cycle attribute owned by business, not a specific period end date for a charity's lodged financial report; ext.licence.end_date belongs to the licence role.

concepts.definition: The date on which the ACNC received the charity's financial report for the reporting period. A document lodgement receipt date, distinct from the AIS receipt date and from the report's period dates.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers financial-report lodgement receipt; dyn.charity.ais_received_date in this patch refers to the AIS lodgement, a different document, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: The type of financial statement the charity lodged with the ACNC, e.g. special purpose or general purpose financial statements (including simplified disclosure variants). A reporting-framework classification, not a legal form or entity type.
values: General purpose financial statements - simplified disclosure
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept describes the accounting framework of a lodged financial statement; entity.entity_type and ext.entity.legal_form describe legal structure, not reporting basis.

concepts.definition: Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity's financial report for the reporting period carries a modification (y/n). A report-quality indicator, not a registration or compliance status.
concepts.why_not_existing: dyn.charity.registration_status is a regulator registration state; no shortlisted concept records whether a lodged financial report was modified.

concepts.definition: Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity's financial report is consolidated with more than one entity (y/n). A reporting-scope indicator, not evidence of group structure or ownership.
source_paths: report consolidated with more than one entity
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept records whether a charity's financial report is consolidated; entity types and relationships are out of scope here and this is a reporting attribute of the charity role.

concepts.definition: The accounting basis (Cash or Accrual) on which the charity prepared its reported financial information for the reporting period, as published by the ACNC. A reporting-basis classification, not a financial measure.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept describes the accounting basis of reported financials; dyn.charity.financial_statement_type in this patch covers the statement framework, a different attribute.

concepts.definition: Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity conducted any activities during its reporting period, recorded as y/n. A 'n' answer is accompanied by a free-text reason in a separate field and is not evidence the charity is inactive or deregistered.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept records whether a charity conducted activities in its reporting period; dyn.charity.registration_status is a regulator status and ext.entity.sector_tag is an activity tag, so reuse would change meaning and owner.

concepts.definition: Free-text explanation supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement for why it did not conduct activities during the reporting period. Publisher wording is retained verbatim; it is self-reported narrative, not a regulator finding.
source_paths: why charity did not conduct activities
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept holds charity self-reported narrative reasons for inactivity; ext.licence.authorisation_text is licence authorisation text owned by the licence role, so reuse would change meaning and owner.

concepts.definition: Free-text description supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement of how it pursued its charitable purposes during the reporting period. Self-reported narrative retained verbatim, not a regulator classification or an ANZSIC activity code.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.sector_tag is a short source-stated tag with a scheme qualifier, not a full narrative description of how purposes were pursued; ext.entity.industry_code is a reviewed crosswalk code. Reuse would change meaning and granularity.

concepts.definition: Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity undertook international activities by operating overseas including programs during the reporting period, recorded as y/n.
source_paths: international activities undertaken - operating overseas including programs
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.operating_region and ext.entity.operating_country describe where a business says it operates, not a charity's self-reported international-activity flag; reuse would change owner, meaning and units (region/country values versus y/n).

concepts.definition: Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity undertook international activities by transferring goods or services overseas during the reporting period, recorded as y/n.
source_paths: international activities undertaken - transferring goods or services overseas
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept captures a charity's self-reported goods/services transfer overseas flag; ext.entity.operating_country is a country value owned by business, so reuse would change meaning, owner and units.

concepts.definition: Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity undertook other international activities not covered by the operating-overseas or goods/services-transfer categories during the reporting period, recorded as y/n.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers a residual 'other international activities' flag for a charity; the existing operating-region/country concepts are business-owned location values, not y/n activity flags.

concepts.definition: Free-text description supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement of the international activities it undertook during the reporting period. Self-reported narrative retained verbatim; it does not by itself establish a country of operation.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.operating_country is a single country value owned by business; this is charity-owned free-text narrative that may mention several places without being a structured country claim, so reuse would change meaning, owner and units.

concepts.definition: Free-text description supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement of the 'other' international activities it undertook during the reporting period. Self-reported narrative retained verbatim.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept holds charity-owned free-text describing residual international activities; ext.entity.operating_country is a structured business-owned country value, so reuse would change meaning, owner and units.

concepts.definition: Publisher-assigned fundraising registration or licence number held by a charity for a specific Australian state or territory, taken verbatim from that jurisdiction's fundraising-number column. Formats differ by jurisdiction (e.g. CH2136, CCP2996, C/10450, FR0017060, CFN/26748) and are not normalised across states; a placeholder value such as 00000 is retained as published and is not evidence of a valid registration.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.number is owned by the licence role and identifies a business-held licence; a state fundraising registration is owned by the fundraising_authorisation role and is jurisdiction-qualified, so reuse would change owner and meaning. dyn.charity.state_association_number is an incorporated-association number, a different registration regime, and is owned by charity.

concepts.definition: Publisher-recorded y/n flag from the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity reported fundraising activity in a given jurisdiction or online, qualified by the jurisdiction (or 'online' for the national online-fundraising column). A 'y' flag is a self-reported activity indicator and does not by itself prove a registration number exists.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept records a charity's per-jurisdiction or online fundraising activity flag; ext.licence.authorisation is licence-owned authorisation text, and address.state is a business address state, so reuse would change owner, meaning and units.

concepts.definition: Number of people the charity reports in its ACNC Annual Information Statement as staff of a given employment category (full time, part time or casual) for its own reporting period. A headcount of people, not full-time-equivalent staff and not a monetary amount; a reported zero is retained as published and is not evidence of no activity.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept records charity staff headcounts; ext.financial.total_income is a monetary business-owned measure and employee expenses is a money amount, so reuse would change meaning, owner and units. The three columns share one meaning (people per employment category) and differ only by category, so one concept with an employment_category qualifier avoids needless aliases.

concepts.definition: Number of volunteers the charity reports in its ACNC Annual Information Statement for its own reporting period. A count of volunteers, distinct from paid staff headcount and from full-time-equivalent staff; a reported zero is retained as published.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers volunteer numbers; dyn.charity.staff_headcount (proposed) covers paid staff by employment category, and volunteers are unpaid and reported in a separate column, so folding them in would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Total full-time-equivalent staff the charity reports in its ACNC Annual Information Statement for its own reporting period, expressed as an FTE number of persons (decimal, e.g. 4.14). This is a workload-equivalent measure, not a headcount and not a monetary amount.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept holds an FTE measure; dyn.charity.staff_headcount (proposed) counts people per employment category and cannot represent fractional FTE, so reuse would change units and meaning.

concepts.definition: Australian Business Number. Has a checksum — validate it, do not just length-check.
As registered. Not the trading name.
Registrable host of a published website (www. removed).

Charity-reported number of full-time staff; staff_headcount covers full/part/casual with an employment_category qualifier. Counts are plain integers; the reporting window comes from the charity's own fin report from/to dates, not calendar 2024.

contract.definition: The accounting basis (Cash or Accrual) on which the charity prepared its reported financial information for the reporting period, as published by the ACNC. A reporting-basis classification, not a financial measure.

The date by which the charity's Annual Information Statement for the reporting year is due to be lodged with the ACNC, as published in the AIS dataset. This is a regulatory lodgement deadline, not a licence or registration date.

The date on which the ACNC received the charity's Annual Information Statement for the reporting year, as published in the AIS dataset. This is a lodgement receipt date, not the charity's establishment or registration date.
Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity is a basic religious charity for the reporting year, recorded as y/n in the source.

Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity conducted any activities during its reporting period, recorded as y/n. A 'n' answer is accompanied by a free-text reason in a separate field and is not evidence the charity is inactive or deregistered.

Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity submitted its financial report to a cooperative or other regulator rather than to the ACNC (y/n), as recorded in the 'coop financial report submitted to regulator' column. A lodgement-channel indicator, not a registration status; the exact regulator and whether it replaces ACNC lodgement are not asserted.

The end date of the reporting period covered by the charity's financial report as lodged with the ACNC. Defines the period scope for the charity's financial figures; it is not a financial year-end attribute or a licence end date.

The start date of the reporting period covered by the charity's financial report as lodged with the ACNC. Defines the period scope for the charity's financial figures; it is not a registration or licence start date.
The date on which the ACNC received the charity's financial report for the reporting period. A document lodgement receipt date, distinct from the AIS receipt date and from the report's period dates.

The type of financial statement the charity lodged with the ACNC, e.g. special purpose or general purpose financial statements (including simplified disclosure variants). A reporting-framework classification, not a legal form or entity type.
values: General purpose financial statements - simplified disclosure

contract.definition: Total full-time-equivalent staff the charity reports in its ACNC Annual Information Statement for its own reporting period, expressed as an FTE number of persons (decimal, e.g. 4.14). This is a workload-equivalent measure, not a headcount and not a monetary amount.

Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity is an incorporated association, recorded as y/n. This is a self-reported association attribute, not an inference of legal form from the charity name.

Free-text description supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement of the international activities it undertook during the reporting period. Self-reported narrative retained verbatim; it does not by itself establish a country of operation.

Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity undertook international activities by operating overseas including programs during the reporting period, recorded as y/n.

Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity undertook other international activities not covered by the operating-overseas or goods/services-transfer categories during the reporting period, recorded as y/n.

Flag published in the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity undertook international activities by transferring goods or services overseas during the reporting period, recorded as y/n.

Free-text explanation supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement for why it did not conduct activities during the reporting period. Publisher wording is retained verbatim; it is self-reported narrative, not a regulator finding.

Free-text description supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement of the 'other' international activities it undertook during the reporting period. Self-reported narrative retained verbatim.

Free-text description supplied by the charity in its ACNC Annual Information Statement of how it pursued its charitable purposes during the reporting period. Self-reported narrative retained verbatim, not a regulator classification or an ANZSIC activity code.

The ACNC registration status of the charity as published in the Annual Information Statement, including revocation reasons such as voluntary revocation or double defaulter. This is a charity-regulator status, not a company legal status or a licence status.
values: Voluntarily Revoked Not Entitled To Be A Charity

contract.definition: Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity's financial report is consolidated with more than one entity (y/n). A reporting-scope indicator, not evidence of group structure or ownership.

Flag published by the ACNC indicating whether the charity's financial report for the reporting period carries a modification (y/n). A report-quality indicator, not a registration or compliance status.

The type of modification the auditor or reviewer applied to the charity's financial report, as published by the ACNC (e.g. qualified/qualification, disclaimed/disclaimer, adverse). Only meaningful where the report modification flag is y; unlisted source labels are withheld rather than guessed.

The ACNC charity size classification (Small, Medium or Large) reported for the charity in its Annual Information Statement. This is a regulator reporting classification, not a measure of company scale, revenue band or legal form.

Number of people the charity reports in its ACNC Annual Information Statement as staff of a given employment category (full time, part time or casual) for its own reporting period. A headcount of people, not full-time-equivalent staff and not a monetary amount; a reported zero is retained as published and is not evidence of no activity.

State or territory incorporated-association registration number held by the charity, qualified by the jurisdiction whose association-number column supplied it. Values are publisher-formatted strings (e.g. INC9886754, A0005374L) and are not normalised across states.

Number of volunteers the charity reports in its ACNC Annual Information Statement for its own reporting period. A count of volunteers, distinct from paid staff headcount and from full-time-equivalent staff; a reported zero is retained as published.

Publisher-recorded y/n flag from the ACNC Annual Information Statement indicating whether the charity reported fundraising activity in a given jurisdiction or online, qualified by the jurisdiction (or 'online' for the national online-fundraising column). A 'y' flag is a self-reported activity indicator and does not by itself prove a registration number exists.

Publisher-assigned fundraising registration or licence number held by a charity for a specific Australian state or territory, taken verbatim from that jurisdiction's fundraising-number column. Formats differ by jurisdiction (e.g. CH2136, CCP2996, C/10450, FR0017060, CFN/26748) and are not normalised across states; a placeholder value such as 00000 is retained as published and is not evidence of a valid registration.
Australian Business Number. Has a checksum — validate it, do not just length-check.
As registered. Not the trading name.
Registrable host of a published website (www. removed).

source_row.international activities details: Mission Without Borders operates internationally through local staff and volunteers in each of the countries where we work. Local staff are trained to international standards and are accountable to both local and international leadership. source_row.how purposes were pursued: The Flicker of Hope Foundation Ltd (FOH) aims to raise much needed funds to support research into and awareness of NF.  FOH contributes funds raised to support researchers in their quest to find positive treatments and solutions to improve the quality of life for those impacted by NF.   FOH through its fund raising efforts has helped to raise awareness in the community of NF.   FOH has made great progress in achieving its aims over the past five years. FoH has raised over $3,000,000 in this period to support the following research projects into NF: >TiNT trial   a trial of trametinib in children and adolescents with NF1 to treat plexiform neurofibromas and optic pathway gliomas. This research is being conducted by the Murdoch Children s Research Institute. >ctDNA NF1 project   a project to explore the feasibility of early detection of Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumours (MPNSTs) using a blood test. Partnering in this project are The Royal Children s Hospital, The Royal Melbourne Hospital and Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre. >Blood Pressure Monitoring   Joint research project between The Royal Children s Hospital and Murdoch Children s Research Institute for blood pressure monitoring of children and adolescents with NF. >FOH initiative, collaborating with The Florey Institute of Neuroscience and Mental Health to conduct world leading, ground breaking research into autism, cognitive and behavioural issues in people with NF1. >Researching for an NF cure   Associate Professor Aaron Schindeler is heading up a new research project aiming to achieve a CURE for NF. The project is being led by a team of researchers from The Children s Hospital at Westmead, Children s Medical Research Institute and The Australian National University. This is an exciting research project for the NF community. >A pioneering NF2 medical research project   Dr Jim Whittle from The Walter and Eliza Hall Institute is establishing a registry of information of Australian patients with NF2 vestibular schwannomas (or acoustic neuromas) and other tumours. This registry will provide a framework to conduct clinical trials and identify new treatments, including evaluating the use of Bevacizumab in Australian patients with acoustic neuromas. >Reproductive decision making  Research led by RNSH NF Team aimed at supporting reproductive decision making for people with NF.  FOH continues to explore opportunities to work with researchers to identify positive treatments and solution to help improve the quality of life for those impacted by NF.

source_row.other international activities descripti: Samaritan's Purse Australia sent Medical and Non-medical volunteers to help with Disaster Relief in affected countries
source_row.how purposes were pursued: Samaritan s Purse is a notforprofit, Christian organisation providing emergency relief and development assistance to suffering people around the world. Samaritan s Purse is meeting the physical needs of victims of war, famine, natural disaster, poverty and disease with the aim of demonstrating God s love and sharing the Good News of Jesus Christ. The aid and assistance are given without regard to the race, creed, gender, religion, or ethnicity of the beneficiaries. We do fundraising by means of social media, mailed and emailed newsletters and appeals as well as visiting churches and private schools. Funds are used to benefit people in developing countries with the following types of work: Education  building of schools and training of teachers, literacy programs etc. Health building of clinics, training locals in health projects, sending medical teams from Australia Disaster Relief sending staff, volunteers and funding to countries affected by serious natural and manmade disasters Protection programs to train vulnerable people on how to migrate safely, programs to help returned migrants who have been exploited, training of villagers to earn incomes so as to avoid the necessity of migration Water providing communities access to clean water sources, build latrines and provide communities with hygiene training. Livelihoods the training of villagers on how best to raise farm animals and plant crops to create sustainability. In Australia we provide disaster relief in disasteraffected areas. We mobilise volunteers and staff to attend as second responders after a disaster.

sampling.sampling: Reservoir of up to 600 rows; first twelve byte-preview rows retained in discovery. Duplicate-content rows share one partition and are deduplicated.

inspection.grain: One row per employer reporting unit for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting, identified by employer name plus Employer ABN; the sheet also carries a second, contextual 2023-24 comparison block of four GPG columns per row, so a row is an employer-year-pair record rather than a single-year measure.
identity_cautions: Employer name is not a unique key: names repeat across sheets and can collide across entities; bind identity on Employer ABN, which is a reporting identifier, not proof of legal form or company-wide scope.
The '2. Employers ' sheet name has a trailing space and must be preserved exactly; do not trim it.
Rows 1-3 are title/context rows (title, 'Results based on 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting', and a year-group header row); the real header is row 4, hence skip_rows=3.

The header has two year groups: columns F-I are 2024-25 (unlabelled suffix) and columns J-M are 2023-24 (headers carry a trailing space). The 2023-24 columns are contextual comparison values, not the current reporting year, and must not be merged with the 2024-25 measures.
Duplicate-looking header labels ('Average total remuneration GPG (%)' etc.) appear twice; disambiguate by year group, not by position alone.
GPG and % women values are stored as decimal fractions (e.g. 0.244 = 24.4%), not as whole percentages; do not multiply or relabel without noting the storage convention.
Blank cells in the 2023-24 block mean the employer had no prior-year comparison, not zero gap.
Employer size range ('<250', '250-499') is a band, not an exact headcount; remuneration figures are pay, not revenue or business income.

This sheet is employer-level results; the '3. Corporate groups ' and '4. Corporate group info' sheets are separate grains (group measures and group-to-employer membership) and must not be joined as if employer rows were group rows.
The 'How to use the GPG Spreadsheet' sheet is documentation and must not be used as a data reader.
inspection.rationale: Byte inspection shows a valid XLSX (magic 504b0304) with five sheets. The '2. Employers ' sheet is the employer-level results table: rows 1-3 are title and year-group context, row 4 is the header, and data begins at row 5, so skip_rows=3 with the exact sheet name (including trailing space). The header spans two year groups (2024-25 in F-I, 2023-24 in J-M), which is why the grain is described as employer with a contextual prior-year block. No nested singleton objects are present in this tabular sheet, so no bindings are proposed. Identity rests on Employer ABN rather than name, and percentage columns are decimal fractions. Documentation and corporate-group sheets are excluded from this reader.

findings: Identity, sector, ANZSIC division/class and reporting name/ABN mappings are semantically defensible: they are owned by the reporting unit, not asserted as legal-person attributes, and the ABN is treated as a reporting identifier rather than proof of legal form or company-wide scope.

The size_band enum is incomplete relative to the observed source vocabulary: held-out validation shows '5000+' present in 5 of 121 records, all rejected as ENUM_UNMAPPED (error_rate_of_present 0.041, coverage 0.959). This is a mapping/ontology defect, not a deliberate abstention.
The grain statement correctly notes the dual-year block (2024-25 in F-I, 2023-24 in J-M) and the group correctly excludes those measure columns, so no year-mixing claim is emitted.
The reader (sheet '2. Employers ' with trailing space, skip_rows=3) and the identity caution that name is non-unique and ABN is the binding identifier are consistent with the held-out rows.
No legal-form, incorporation-date, revenue-as-income or group-scope claims are emitted; the concepts explicitly disclaim these, which is correct.

The 'why_not_existing' text for anzsic_division and anzsic_class repeats 'ext.entity.industry_code and entity.industry_code' — a duplicated reference that should name the two distinct existing concepts it is distinguishing from.
semantic_risks: size_band enum omits the '5000+' band that the publisher uses, so the largest employers are silently dropped rather than represented; this understates coverage of the top band and could bias any downstream size analysis.
The size_band definition lists only four example bands; if the enum is extended, the definition should state that the band set is publisher-defined and open-ended at the top.

ANZSIC division/class are stored as name labels, not codes; downstream consumers must not treat them as coded ANZSIC values — the definitions say this, but the risk remains if joined to coded industry data.

ABN transform validates checksum but does not establish that the ABN belongs to the legal person; the concept correctly scopes it to the reporting unit, but any join to entity.abn would be an unsupported identity claim.
checked_reuse: entity.legal_name / entity.trading_name — correctly not reused; source is a reporting label, not a verified legal/trading name.
entity.abn — correctly not reused; source ABN is a reporting-unit submission identifier, not asserted as the business legal person's ABN.
ext.entity.sector_tag — correctly not reused; WGEA private/public sector is a reporting classification, not a scheme-tagged activity/beneficiary tag.
ext.financial.revenue_band — correctly not reused; employee-count band is not a revenue band.
ext.entity.industry_code / entity.industry_code — correctly not reused for name labels; coded ANZSIC values differ in type and meaning.
critic.rationale: The group's emitted claims are semantically sound for identity, sector, industry labels and reporting name/ABN, and correctly avoid legal-form, revenue and group-scope overreach. The one blocking defect is the incomplete size_band enum: held-out validation shows the publisher's '5000+' band is present and rejected as ENUM_UNMAPPED in 5 records, so the enum must be extended (and the definition updated) rather than left as a silent coverage gap. A secondary non-blocking cleanup is the duplicated 'ext.entity.industry_code and entity.industry_code' reference in the ANZSIC why_not_existing text. Repair is confined to mapping/ontology for size_band; no reader or grain change is required.

blocking_findings.actual: enum values ["<250", "250-499", "500-999", "1000-4999"]; map_enum has no entry for '5000+', producing 5 ENUM_UNMAPPED rejections
blocking_findings.expected: enum includes the publisher's top band '5000+' and map_enum maps '5000+' -> '5000+', so all observed size bands are representable
blocking_findings.evidence: validation_fields for dyn.employer_reporting_unit.size_band: source_present 121, emitted 116, coverage 0.959, errors ENUM_UNMAPPED 5, error_examples ['5000+','5000+','5000+','5000+']; quality.malformed_reasons ENUM_UNMAPPED 5

Re-run validation and confirm size_band coverage reaches 1.0 with zero ENUM_UNMAPPED.

findings: All six group fields are identity/scope qualifiers owned by the reporting unit, not measures; no GPG, remuneration or % women columns are claimed by this group, so the employer-vs-corporate-group grain caution is respected.

Semantic separation is defensible: reporting_name/reporting_abn are reporting-unit labels and identifiers, explicitly not legal name, trading name, legal form or company-wide scope; sector is a WGEA private/public reporting classification, not a legal form; size_band is an employee-count band, not a headcount or revenue band; anzsic_division/anzsic_class are publisher name labels, not coded ANZSIC values.

Held-out validation shows 121/121 source-present and emitted for every field with 0.0 error rate of present values; the two held-out examples (ordinals 13 and 38) show values matching raw source strings after trim/collapse_whitespace, and enum values ('Private', '<250', '250-499') are within the declared value sets.

The abn transform is applied to Employer ABN and the held-out examples (47128389480, 47065021463) are 11-digit values; the concept definition correctly frames this as a reporting identifier that does not establish legal form or company-wide scope.

Reader configuration matches the documented inspection: exact sheet name '2. Employers ' with trailing space, skip_rows=3, no record_path, no bindings; documentation and corporate-group sheets are excluded.

Grain statement honestly describes the row as an employer-year-pair record carrying a contextual 2023-24 block, and the group does not emit those prior-year columns, so no year-group merge risk is introduced by this group.
No population accuracy claim is made; quality note explicitly states the gate does not establish semantic truth or useful coverage, and semantic_precision is null rather than asserted.

No AI decision is labelled as human review; no invented fallback dates are demanded; missing required context is treated as deliberate abstention (0 withheld here, consistent with full source presence).
semantic_risks: size_band enum is declared closed with five values; if the publisher uses any additional band label (e.g. a different top band or a 'Not stated' value), map_enum with passthrough=false and default=null will silently drop it rather than surface an unmapped reason. This is a coverage risk, not a demonstrated semantic error in the held-out evidence.

anzsic_division and anzsic_class are typed as free strings holding publisher labels; downstream consumers must not treat them as coded ANZSIC values or join them to coded industry_code without a separate crosswalk.
reporting_abn is a reporting identifier; it must not be used as a proxy for the business legal person's ABN or to infer legal form, and the concept definition already states this.
sector enum is limited to 'Private'/'Public'; any other publisher sector label would be dropped by the closed map_enum, again a coverage rather than semantic risk in the observed evidence.
checked_reuse: entity.legal_name / entity.trading_name rejected for Employer name: source is a reporting label, not a verified legal or trading name; owner and meaning differ.
entity.abn rejected for Employer ABN: source is the reporting unit's submission identifier, not an assertion of the business legal person's ABN.

ext.entity.industry_code and entity.industry_code rejected for ANZSIC Division/Class columns: those expect coded ANZSIC values owned by business; source holds publisher name labels for the reporting unit.
ext.entity.sector_tag rejected for Sector: that is a scheme-qualified activity/beneficiary tag owned by business; source is a WGEA private/public reporting classification of the reporting unit.
ext.financial.revenue_band rejected for Employer size range: revenue band under a named scheme is not an employee-count band; reuse would change meaning.
critic.rationale: The group emits only identity and scope qualifiers for the WGEA employer reporting unit, with definitions that correctly separate reporting labels from legal names, reporting identifiers from legal-person ABNs, employee-count bands from headcounts and revenue bands, and publisher ANZSIC name labels from coded industry values. Held-out validation shows full source-present coverage (121/121) with zero error rate of present values across all six fields, and the two held-out examples confirm values match raw source strings and declared enum sets. Reader configuration matches the documented sheet name, skip_rows and exclusion of documentation and corporate-group sheets, and the grain statement honestly describes the contextual prior-year block without emitting it. No blocking semantic, ownership, unit, date, legal-claim or provenance defect is evidenced. Residual risks are closed-enum coverage for size_band and sector and the need to treat ANZSIC labels and reporting_abn as non-coded, non-legal identifiers; these are documented cautions rather than demonstrated errors, so the verdict is accept with repair_scope none.

findings: Semantics of the four proposed concepts are defensible: they are gender pay gaps (not pay levels, not business income), owned by employer_reporting_unit, with the decimal-fraction storage convention and negative-favouring-women direction stated explicitly.
Year-group disambiguation is correct: the 2024-25 block (F-I) is consumed and the 2023-24 block (J-M) is explicitly unmapped with a period reason, so the duplicate header labels are not merged.

Identity handling is sound: Employer ABN plus Employer name as key_paths, with an explicit caution that ABN is a reporting identifier and not proof of legal form or group-wide scope; no legal-form or consolidated-scope claim is made.
Grain is honestly described as an employer-year-pair record because each row carries a contextual prior-year block; the group purpose is bounded to 2024-25.
Reader configuration matches inspection: sheet '2. Employers ' with trailing space preserved, skip_rows=3, header at row 4, data from row 5.
Coverage is honestly bounded: 121 validation records per field, 0 emitted, 0 withheld for missing context, and the quality note does not claim semantic truth or population accuracy.

However, the technical gate fails: every present value is rejected as INVALID_DECIMAL_INVALID (484/484, error_rate 1.0), so no claim reaches the ontology despite correct semantics. This is a blocking defect, not a coverage limitation.
semantic_risks: The decimal type rejects the publisher's decimal-fraction strings (e.g. '0.068', '0', '0.221'), so the storage convention is documented but not executable; if the type is loosened carelessly, whole-percentage relabelling could be introduced.
Zero values ('0') are legitimate zero gaps, not missing data; any coercion that treats 0 or blank alike would misstate the measure.

The 2023-24 block is correctly unmapped, but the unmapped source_paths use synthetic '_2' suffixes; if the reader ever renames duplicate headers, the unmapped reasons could silently stop matching the actual columns.
Period is carried as a literal qualifier because no date column exists; this is acceptable, but it must not be described as a publisher-stated claim period.
Total remuneration is pay, not revenue; the definitions say so, but downstream joins to financial income concepts must not be inferred from the word 'remuneration'.

critic.rationale: The group's semantic modelling is largely correct: the four concepts are genuine gender pay gaps owned by the employer reporting unit, the decimal-fraction convention and negative-direction meaning are stated, the 2024-25 versus 2023-24 year groups are separated with explicit unmapped reasons, identity rests on ABN plus name without inferring legal form or group scope, and the grain honestly notes the prior-year block. Coverage is honestly bounded at 121 validation records with no invented fallback dates. The blocking problem is executable, not semantic: the decimal type rejects every present value as INVALID_DECIMAL_INVALID (484/484, error_rate 1.0, passes_technical_gate false), so the documented storage convention is not actually applied and zero emitted observations result. Because an accepting verdict with blocking findings would be rejected, and because the defect is a concrete mapping/type correction rather than a hypothetical feature, the verdict is reject with repair_scope both: the decimal parsing must accept the publisher's decimal-fraction strings (including '0') without relabelling to whole percentages, and the concept type/definition must remain consistent with that executable behaviour.

Units are handled correctly: publisher decimal fractions are parsed as decimals with no multiplication or whole-percentage relabelling, and '0' is preserved as a legitimate zero gap rather than nulled.

Year-group disambiguation is correct: the 2024-25 block (F-I) is consumed and the duplicate-labelled 2023-24 block is explicitly unmapped with a defensible reason, so the period qualifier '2024-25' is not misstated.

Identity is bound on Employer ABN plus Employer name with an explicit caution that ABN is a reporting identifier, not proof of legal form or company-wide scope; no legal-form or group-scope claim is made.

Corporate-group and documentation sheets are excluded from the reader, and the trailing-space sheet name '2. Employers ' is preserved.
No date column exists in the source; carrying the reporting year as a literal period qualifier rather than inventing a claim_period or fallback date is an honest, bounded choice, not a defect.
semantic_risks: The 'period' qualifier is a literal string rather than a source-derived date; downstream consumers must not treat it as a publisher-stated effective date.

Grain is described as an employer-year-pair record because of the contextual 2023-24 block; if a future reader consumes both blocks, the single-year period qualifier would need to be split per year group.
Employer name collisions across sheets remain a latent risk if identity is ever re-bound on name alone; current binding on ABN mitigates this.
Negative GPG values (gap favouring women) are documented but not separately validated in the held-out sample; sign handling should be spot-checked if negative rows appear.

concepts.definition: The employer size range band reported for the WGEA submission, expressed as an employee-count band such as '<250', '250-499' or '5000+'. The band set is publisher-defined and open-ended at the top; it is a band, not an exact headcount.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents an employer headcount band; ext.financial.revenue_band is a revenue band under a named scheme and is not an employee-count band, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: The ANZSIC division name the employer reporting unit reported for its WGEA submission, e.g. 'Transport, Postal and Warehousing'. It is the publisher's division label, not a coded ANZSIC value.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.industry_code expects a coded ANZSIC value (division letter, subdivision, group or class) and is owned by business; entity.industry_code likewise expects a coded ANZSIC value for the business. This column holds a division name label for the reporting unit, so type, meaning and owner differ from both.

concepts.definition: The ANZSIC class name the employer reporting unit reported for its WGEA submission, e.g. 'Computer System Design and Related Services'. It is the publisher's class label, not a coded ANZSIC class number.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.industry_code expects a coded ANZSIC value and is owned by business; entity.industry_code likewise expects a coded ANZSIC value for the business. This column holds a class name label for the reporting unit, so type, meaning and owner differ from both.

concepts.definition: The employer name as stated by the employer reporting unit in its WGEA Gender Equality Reporting submission for the reporting year. This is the reporting label, not a verified legal name or trading name, and is not a unique identifier.
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.legal_name and entity.trading_name are owned by business and assert a legal/trading status this source does not establish; the value here is a reporting-unit label for a WGEA submission, so owner and meaning differ.

concepts.definition: The ABN the employer reporting unit used to identify itself in its WGEA Gender Equality Reporting submission. It is a reporting identifier for the reporting unit and does not by itself establish legal form or company-wide scope.
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.abn is owned by business and asserts the ABN of the business legal person; here the ABN is the reporting unit's submission identifier, so owner and scope differ even though the value format is the same.

concepts.definition: The sector classification the employer reporting unit reported for its WGEA submission, distinguishing private from public sector employers. It is a reporting classification, not a legal form.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.sector_tag is a source-stated activity/beneficiary tag requiring a scheme qualifier and is owned by business; this is a WGEA private/public sector classification of the reporting unit, so meaning and owner differ.

concepts.definition: The share of the employer reporting unit's total workforce who were women, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.244 = 24.4%), not a whole percentage; it is a workforce composition share, not a pay gap.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a female workforce composition share; ext.financial.revenue_band and the GPG concepts concern revenue bands and pay gaps, so reuse would change meaning. Owner is the reporting unit, not the business.
